title: CDS Full Length Mock Test 02 (Hard Level)
description: Combined Defence Services Examination style full-length mock covering English, Elementary Mathematics and General Knowledge. Hard level, 100 questions.
instructions: There is a penalty of 0.83 marks for every wrong answer.
No marks will be deducted for unattempted questions.
Choose the most appropriate option among the four given choices.
The paper covers English, Elementary Mathematics and General Knowledge as in CDS.
Use of calculator or electronic device is not permitted.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the part that contains an error: Each of the soldiers / were given / a new set of / combat uniforms.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb; use 'was given'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the error: The news / are spreading / faster than / expected.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and singular; use 'is spreading'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the error: He is one of those officers / who has / always put / duty first.
options: He is one of those officers
questions.explanation: Antecedent of 'who' is 'officers' (plural); use 'who have'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The battalion was _____ to hold the ridge at all costs.
questions.explanation: 'Ordered to' is the standard military collocation for a binding directive.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: His testimony was so _____ that the court discarded it.
questions.explanation: Incoherent means unclear and disjointed, so it would be discarded.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the synonym of OBDURATE.
questions.explanation: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change opinion.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the synonym of PERNICIOUS.
questions.explanation: Pernicious means causing serious harm, especially gradually.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the antonym of BENIGN.
questions.explanation: Benign means harmless/kind; malignant is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the antonym of PAUCITY.
questions.explanation: Paucity means scarcity; abundance is the antonym.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the improved form: He suggested that the plan is revised immediately.
questions.explanation: After 'suggested that', the subjunctive 'be revised' is required.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the improved form: Hardly he had entered the camp when the alarm sounded.
options: Hardly had he entered the camp when
Hardly he entered the camp than
questions.explanation: Inversion is required after 'Hardly': Hardly had he...

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Change to passive: The general awarded the soldiers gallantry medals.
options: The soldiers were awarded gallantry medals by the general.
The soldiers awarded medals by general.
questions.explanation: Object 'soldiers' becomes subject; past simple becomes 'were awarded'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He said, 'I will report at dawn.' Change to indirect speech.
options: He said that he would report at dawn.
He said that he will report at dawn.
He said that I would report at dawn.
He said he reports at dawn.
questions.explanation: In reported speech 'will' becomes 'would' and pronoun shifts to 'he'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The convoy moved _____ the river under cover of darkness.
questions.explanation: 'Along the river' means following its course.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The talks _____ after both sides refused to compromise.
questions.explanation: 'Break down' of talks means they failed/collapsed.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correctly used sentence.
options: The number of casualties was higher than expected.
The number of casualties were higher than expected.
A number of casualty was high.
Number of the casualties are high.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb.

questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'sailors' (plural): were.
